title: Cultural Adaptation in Large Language Models for Political Discourse

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating cultural failure modes (e.g., concept collapse, pragmatic misreading) using curated diagnostic sets with local annotators, expert adjudication protocols for concept mapping tasks across different institutional contexts, and human evaluation rubrics assessing cultural fidelity and meaning preservation.

Calculating disaggregated performance metrics by language and dialect, evaluating models under translation and code-switching conditions, and measuring calibration error and disparity ratios between dominant and minority language groups (e.g., comparing performance on German vs. Italian inputs).

Conducting audit-style evaluations with group-conditioned error rates to detect disproportionate flagging, differential visibility, or systematic delegitimation of specific publics, as well as applying cross-lingual stance detection to assess how consistently political concepts are treated across different political systems.
